claim: MAP6-immunoaffinity chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry identified twelve specific peptides belonging to CRMP2, three specific peptides from CRMP4, two specific peptides from CRMP1, and six peptides shared by two or three of these CRMP proteins.
source: More precisely, we identified twelve specific peptides belonging to CRMP2, three specific peptides from CRMP4, two specific peptides from CRMP1, and six peptides shared by two or three of these CRMP proteins (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data from MAP6-immunoaffinity chromatography experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: MAP6 directly binds to CRMP1, CRMP2, and CRMP4.
source: Purified MAP6-N bound directly to CRMP1, CRMP2, and CRMP4 (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by pull-down experiments shown in Figure 1B using purified recombinant proteins.

claim: Downregulation of CRMP2 weakly stimulates axonal growth (108%, p = 0.0275).
source: Decreased expression of CRMP2 weakly stimulated axonal growth (108%, p = 0.0275), knockdown of CRMP1 showed the same tendency but the increase was not significant (106%, p = 0.0976).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of axonal length in cultured subicular neurons treated with CRMP2 siRNA.

claim: Downregulation of CRMP4 stimulates basal axonal growth (116%, p = 0.0028).
source: In contrast, axonal-growth stimulation was more pronounced following inhibition of CRMP4 expression (116%, p = 0.0028) (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of axonal length in cultured subicular neurons treated with CRMP4 siRNA.

claim: CRMP4 knockdown completely blocks the response to Sema3E (99%, p > 0.9999).
source: Conversely, CRMP4 knockdown completely blocked the response to Sema3E (Figure 2C and D, 99%, p > 0.9999).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of axonal length in CRMP4 siRNA-treated neurons exposed to Sema3E.

claim: CRMP1 and CRMP2 knockdown do not affect Sema3E's growth-promoting effect.
source: Although treatment with Crmp1 or Crmp2 siRNAs drastically reduced protein expression levels (Figure 2A), the Sema3E growth-promoting effect was still observed (Figure 2D, 119% and 124%, p = 0.0013 and p < 0.0001, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements showing that Sema3E still stimulates axonal growth in neurons treated with CRMP1 or CRMP2 siRNA.

claim: CRMP4-KO neurons exhibit significantly longer axons (147%, p > 0.0004).
source: In accordance with the results from siRNA experiments (Figure 2B), CRMP4-KO neurons exhibited significantly longer axons (Figure 2E, 147%, p > 0.0004) and no longer responded to Sema3E stimulation (Figure 2F, 105%, p = 0.2652).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of axonal length in cultured CRMP4-KO neurons.

claim: CRMP4-KO neurons do not respond to Sema3E stimulation (105%, p = 0.2652).
source: In accordance with the results from siRNA experiments (Figure 2B), CRMP4-KO neurons exhibited significantly longer axons (Figure 2E, 147%, p > 0.0004) and no longer responded to Sema3E stimulation (Figure 2F, 105%, p = 0.2652).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements showing no significant change in axonal length when CRMP4-KO neurons are treated with Sema3E.

claim: Electroporation of CRMP4-KO neurons with CRMP4-eGFP completely restores their response to Sema3E (143%, p < 0.0001).
source: Furthermore, electroporation of CRMP4-KO neurons with CRMP4-eGFP completely restored their response to Sema3E (Figure 2G, 143%, p < 0.0001).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments showing that re-expression of CRMP4 restores Sema3E responsiveness in CRMP4-KO neurons.

claim: CRMP4 is predominantly expressed during embryonic and postnatal development between E17.5 and P7, and levels decline sharply after P14.
source: As reported in the rat brain (Byk et al., 1998), CRMP4 was predominantly expressed during embryonic and postnatal development between embryonic day 17.5 (E17.5) and postnatal day 7 (P7), and levels declined sharply after postnatal day 14 (P14) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data showing CRMP4 expression levels at different developmental stages and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: CRMP4 is expressed in subicular neurons and their axonal projections during post-commissural fornix formation.
source: Taken together, our results indicate that during formation of the post-commissural fornix, CRMP4 is strongly expressed in subicular neurons and in their axonal projections in vivo.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunolabeling data showing CRMP4 expression in subicular neurons and fornix projections.

claim: The diameter of the fornix is reduced by 53% in CRMP4-KO mice at P0 (p = 0.0043).
source: The diameter of the fornix was reduced by 53% in CRMP4-KO mice (Figure 4A, histograms, p = 0.0043).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements of fornix diameter in coronal sections from P0 WT and CRMP4-KO brains.

claim: The diameter of the mammillo-thalamic tract remains unchanged between WT and CRMP4-KO brains (p = 0.7922).
source: In contrast, the diameter of the neighboring mammillo-thalamic tract remained unchanged between WT and KO brains, indicating a specific role of CRMP4 in fornix formation (Figure 4A, histograms, p = 0.7922).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements showing no significant difference in mammillo-thalamic tract diameter between genotypes.

claim: The post-commissural fornix length is 26% shorter in CRMP4-KO brains at P0 (p = 0.0173).
source: The post-commissural fornix length was 26% shorter in CRMP4-KO brains (Figure 4B, histogram, p = 0.0173), appeared less fasciculated than in WT brains, and also presented divergent axons (Figure 4B, observed 3/6 KO, white arrow).
evidence: The claim is supported by measurements of post-commissural fornix length on sagittal sections from P0 brains.

claim: The volume of post-commissural fornices in CRMP4-KO brains is significantly decreased by 40% overall (p = 0.0070), with a 51% reduction at P0 (p = 0.0159).
source: Finally, quantification of the volume of the post-commissural fornix was significantly decreased – by 40% overall – in CRMP4-KO brains (Figure 4C, histogram, WT vs. KO p = 0.0070), with a 51% reduction recorded at P0 (Figure 4C, histogram, p = 0.0159).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D volumetric analysis of post-commissural fornices from cleared whole brains at multiple developmental stages.

claim: In CRMP4-KO mice, the surface area occupied by fibers in the post-commissural fornix progressively decreases in the rostro-caudal region by 30%, 33%, and 47% at three different anatomical planes.
source: In CRMP4-KO mice, the surface area occupied by the fibers in the post-commissural fornix progressively decreased in the rostro-caudal region, by 30%, 33%, and 47% (Figure 5B, C, and D, p = 0.0476, p = 0.0159, p = 0.0159, respectively) compared to the corresponding WT post-commissural fornix.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of gold chloride-stained coronal sections from adult brains at three rostro-caudal planes.

claim: The fornix volume is 31% decreased in Crmp4+/-/Sema3e+/- double mutants compared to WT controls at P0 (p = 0.0061).
source: The fornix volume was 31% decreased in Crmp4+/-/Sema3e+/- double mutants compared to WT controls (Figure 6A and B, p = 0.0061).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D volumetric analysis of segmented fornices from cleared P0 brains of double heterozygous animals.

claim: No significant decrease in fornix volume is observed in Crmp4+/- or Sema3e+/- single mutants (–4% and +2%, p > 0.999 for both).
source: No significant decrease was observed in Crmp4+/- or Sema3e+/- single mutants (Figure 6B, –4% and +2%, p > 0.999 for both).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D volumetric analysis showing no significant difference in fornix volume in single heterozygous animals compared to WT.

claim: CRMP4 interacts with the Sema3E tripartite receptor complex (PlxD1, Nrp1, and VEGFR2).
source: We detected PlxD1, Nrp1, and CRMP4 proteins in VEGFR2 immunoprecipitates, indicating the presence of a complex involving both Sema3E receptor components and CRMP4 (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments in HEK293T/17 cells expressing all four proteins.

claim: CRMP4 interacts with PlxD1 and Nrp1 individually, but not with VEGFR2 alone.
source: VEGFR2 alone did not co-immunoprecipitate with CRMP4-tGFP (Figure 7B), whereas isolated Nrp1 or PlxD1 did (Figure 7C and D). These results strongly suggest that CRMP4 forms a complex with the Sema3E tripartite receptors through interactions with both PlxD1 and Nrp1.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments testing individual receptor-CRMP4 interactions in HEK293T/17 cells.

claim: The interactions between CRMP4 and Sema3E receptors are resistant to concentrations of up to 1% Triton X-100.
source: Indeed, these interactions were even resistant to concentrations of up to 1% Triton X-100 (Figure 8A), suggesting a possible role of DRM domains in their formation.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments performed with different detergent concentrations.

claim: CRMP4, Nrp1, and PlxD1 are found in DRM fractions (PlxD1: 7.7%, Nrp1: 4.3%, CRMP4: 1.6%, flotillin: 53.2%, n = 3).
source: CRMP4, Nrp1, and PlxD1 were also found in the DRM fractions (PlxD1: 7.7%, Nrp1: 4.3%, CRMP4: 1.6%, flotillin: 53.2%, n = 3) but in much lower amounts compared to the membrane fractions (PlxD1: 87.6%, Nrp1: 90.4%, CRMP4: 90.0%, flotillin: 32.4%, n = 3), suggesting that only a small proportion of the Sema3E receptors and CRMP4 locates in DRM (Figure 8B).
evidence: The claim is supported by sucrose-density gradient fractionation experiments of HEK293T/17 cell lysates.

claim: Treatment with 10 mM MβCD for 7 hr results in complete elimination of CRMP4-containing and receptor-containing DRM.
source: Treating cell cultures with 10 mM MβCD for 7 hr resulted in a complete elimination of CRMP4-containing and receptor-containing DRM, and partial reduction of flotillin-containing DRM (Figure 8C).
evidence: The claim is supported by sucrose-density gradient fractionation experiments after MβCD treatment.

claim: The ratio of receptors present in immunoprecipitation relative to CRMP4 is considerably higher in DRM fractions than in RPM fractions (Nrp1 and PlxD1 signals represent 62% and 25% of CRMP4 signal in DRM vs. 0.18% and 0.69% in RPM).
source: Surprisingly, even though the two receptors co-immunoprecipitated with CRMP4 in both RPM and DRM fractions, the ratio of receptors present in the immunoprecipitation relative to the amount of immunoprecipitated CRMP4 was considerably higher in the DRM fraction than in the RPM fraction (Nrp1 and PlxD1 signals represent 62% and 25% of CRMP4 signal, respectively, in DRM fractions, as compared to 0.18% and 0.69% of CRMP4 signal, respectively, in RPM fractions).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments performed on pooled DRM and RPM fractions.

claim: Addition of 1 or 1.5 mM MβCD results in a 1.1-fold increase in axonal length (112% and 115% of control).
source: We first investigated the effect of MβCD on axonal growth, and found, in accordance with previous work (Ko et al., 2005), that the addition of 1 or 1.5 mM of MβCD had a very mild effect, resulting in a 1.1-fold increase in axonal length (Figure 9—figure supplement 1, 112% of control for 1 mM MβCD, and 115% for 1.5 mM).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of axonal length in cultured neurons treated with MβCD and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: Sema3E induces a 1.3-fold increase in axonal length in the absence of MβCD (137% of control, p < 0.0001).
source: Next, Sema3E, in the absence of MβCD, induced an expected 1.3-fold increase in axonal length (Figure 9A and B, 137% of control, p < 0.0001), whereas in the presence of 1.0 and 1.5 mM MβCD, Sema3E no longer stimulated axonal growth (Figure 9A and B, 107% and 101% of control, p = 0.1150 and p > 0.9999, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of axonal length in cultured subicular neurons treated with Sema3E.

claim: In the presence of 1.0 and 1.5 mM MβCD, Sema3E no longer stimulates axonal growth (107% and 101% of control, p = 0.1150 and p > 0.9999).
source: Next, Sema3E, in the absence of MβCD, induced an expected 1.3-fold increase in axonal length (Figure 9A and B, 137% of control, p < 0.0001), whereas in the presence of 1.0 and 1.5 mM MβCD, Sema3E no longer stimulated axonal growth (Figure 9A and B, 107% and 101% of control, p = 0.1150 and p > 0.9999, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements showing that MβCD blocks Sema3E-induced axonal growth.

claim: Sema3E treatment triggers an increase in Akt and GSK3β phosphorylation (203% ± 35% and 153% ± 9.5 of control, respectively).
source: As expected, Sema3E treatment triggered the signaling cascade with an increase in Akt and GSK3β phosphorylation (203% ± 35% and 153% ± 9.5 of the control, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis of phosphorylated Akt and GSK3β in subicular neurons treated with Sema3E.

claim: Sema3E treatment results in a considerable decrease in CRMP4 phosphorylation (43% ± 5.4 of control).
source: In the same experiments, a considerable decrease in CRMP4 phosphorylation (43% ± 5.4 of the control) was observed.
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis of phosphorylated CRMP4 in subicular neurons treated with Sema3E.

claim: MβCD treatment inhibits the basal PI3K/AKT pathway (46% ± 15% and 65% ± 12 of control signal for p-AKT and p-GSK3β, respectively).
source: Depleting cholesterol using MβCD (Ohtsuka et al., 2017; Raghu et al., 2010; Scheinman et al., 2013) inhibits the basal PI3k/AKT pathway (46% ± 15% and 65% ± 12 of control signal for p-AKT and p-GSK3β, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis showing reduced phosphorylation of AKT and GSK3β after MβCD treatment, and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: In the presence of MβCD, application of Sema3E does not lead to increased phosphorylation of p-AKT and p-GSK3β (106% ± 8% and 99% ± 6, respectively), nor to a decrease in CRMP4 phosphorylation (108% ± 8).
source: In the presence of MβCD, the application of Sema3E does not lead to increased phosphorylation of p-AKT and p-GSK3β (106% ± 8% and 99% ± 6, respectively), nor to a decrease in CRMP4 phosphorylation (108% ± 8).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis showing that MβCD blocks Sema3E-induced changes in phosphorylation.

claim: Both CRMP4-4A and CRMP4-4D mutant forms restore axonal growth induced by Sema3E (134% and 141% of control, p < 0.0001 in both cases).
source: Surprisingly, both mutant forms of CRMP4 restored the axonal growth induced by addition of Sema3E (Figure 10B, 134% and 141% of control, respectively, p < 0.0001 in both cases).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments in CRMP4-KO neurons transfected with non-phosphorylatable or phosphomimetic CRMP4 constructs.

claim: CRMP4∆Cyto does not restore Sema3E-induced axonal growth (108% of control, p = 0.1985).
source: CRMP4∆Cyto no longer restored Sema3E-induced axonal growth (Figure 10C, 108% of control, p = 0.1985).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments showing that CRMP4 lacking the cytoskeleton-binding domain cannot restore Sema3E responsiveness.

claim: CRMP4 is a new specific effector of Sema3E-mediated axonal growth.
source: In this study, we characterized CRMP4 as a new specific effector of Sema3E-mediated axonal growth.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple experimental findings including siRNA knockdown, knockout studies, and rescue experiments demonstrating CRMP4's specific role in Sema3E signaling.

claim: MAP6 acts as a scaffold protein within subicular neurons, facilitating the interaction of Sema3E pathway receptors and downstream SH3-containing actors.
source: We have previously proposed that MAP6 acts as a scaffold protein within subicular neurons, facilitating the interaction of Sema3E pathway receptors and downstream SH3-containing actors (Deloulme et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is based on previous work by the authors cited in the manuscript.

claim: CRMP4-KO mice have defects in fornix development that are identical to those reported in Sema3E-KO mice.
source: In addition, CRMP4-KO mice had defects in fornix development that were identical to those reported in Sema3E-KO mice (Chauvet et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by the authors' experimental observations of fornix defects in CRMP4-KO mice and comparison with published data on Sema3E-KO mice.

claim: Crmp4 and Sema3E cooperate to allow the correct establishment of the fornix.
source: Finally, analysis of the fornix in Crmp4/Sema3E double heterozygote animals compared to single heterozygote animals revealed that Crmp4 and Sema3E cooperate to allow the correct establishment of the fornix.
evidence: The claim is supported by genetic interaction studies showing fornix defects in double heterozygous animals but not in single heterozygotes.

claim: Sema3A stimulates the development of dendrites in a CRMP4-dependent manner in hippocampal neurons.
source: Thus, Sema3A stimulates the development of dendrites in a CRMP4-dependent manner (Niisato et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Crmp4 and Sema3d genetically interact to promote axonal growth from some peripheral neuron populations in zebrafish.
source: In addition, Crmp4 and Sema3d genetically interact to promote axonal growth from some peripheral neuron populations in zebrafish (Tanaka et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: CRMP1, CRMP2, and CRMP4 share some cellular functions and may have redundant roles related to their extensive sequence homology (74% to 76%).
source: Thus, CRMP1, CRMP2, and CRMP4 share some cellular functions and may have redundant roles that could be related to their extensive sequence homology, which ranges from 74% to 76% (Charrier et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is based on observations from multiple studies and sequence homology data cited in the manuscript.

claim: CRMP4 plays a specific role in the Sema3E signaling pathway.
source: These results suggest that CRMP4 plays a specific role in this signaling pathway.
evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental results showing that only CRMP4, not CRMP1 or CRMP2, is required for Sema3E signaling.

claim: CRMP4 function is regulated by the molecular context of the neurons where it is expressed.
source: Our research thus contributes to a growing body of work proposing that CRMP4 function is regulated by the molecular context of the neurons where it is expressed (Alabed et al., 2007; Duplan et al., 2010; Girouard et al., 2020; Niisato et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' findings combined with multiple published studies showing context-dependent CRMP4 function.

claim: CRMP4-KO mice display dendritic arborization defects in hippocampal CA1 and cortical pyramidal neurons, mispositioning of Purkinje cells, and olfactory bulb lamination defects.
source: CRMP4-KO mice display dendritic arborization defects in hippocampal CA1 and cortical pyramidal neurons, mispositioning of Purkinje cells, and olfactory bulb lamination defects (Takaya et al., 2017; Tsutiya et al., 2016; Yamazaki et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: A de novo variant of Crmp4 was identified in an adult male with ASD.
source: Moreover, a de novo variant of Crmp4 was recently identified in an adult males with ASD, and CRMP4-KO mice show a decrease in social interaction as well as a severe alterations to their sensory responses (Tsutiya et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: CRMP4-KO mice show a decrease in social interaction and severe alterations to their sensory responses.
source: Moreover, a de novo variant of Crmp4 was recently identified in an adult males with ASD, and CRMP4-KO mice show a decrease in social interaction as well as a severe alterations to their sensory responses (Tsutiya et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Complex formation between CRMP1, CRMP2, and CRMP4, and PlxA1 has been known for several years.
source: Complex formation between CRMP1, CRMP2, and CRMP4, and PlxA1 – a Sema3A co-receptor – has been known for several years (Deo et al., 2004; Schmidt et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: The direct interaction of CRMP2 with PlxA3 is involved in dendritic growth under the control of Sema3A.
source: More recently, a study showed that the direct interaction of CRMP2 with PlxA3 was involved in dendritic growth under the control of Sema3A (Jiang et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Binding of CRMP2 to the Ngr1 receptor and PlxA2 induced by Nogo-A limits axonal regrowth after injury.
source: Binding of CRMP2 to the Ngr1 receptor and PlxA2 induced by Nogo-A was also demonstrated to limit axonal regrowth after injury (Sekine et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: In leukemic T cells, Sema3A/Fas-dependent apoptosis requires Nrp1 and plexin-A1 to co-localize within lipid rafts.
source: For example, in leukemic T cells, Sema3A/Fas-dependent apoptosis requires Nrp1 and plexin-A1 to co-localize within lipid rafts (Moretti et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Lipid rafts are involved in Sema3A-induced growth cone collapse in neurons following the recruitment of Nrp1 to the rafts.
source: Lipid rafts are also involved in Sema3A-induced growth cone collapse in neurons following the recruitment of Nrp1 to the rafts (Guirland et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: The presence of CRMP4 in membrane domains has been implicated in the maintenance of growth cones.
source: The presence of CRMP4 in membrane domains has been implicated in the maintenance of growth cones, suggesting that this localization places CRMP4 in an environment containing specific signaling proteins and cytoskeletal elements (Rosslenbroich et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Cerebral ischemia induced by occlusion leads to CRMP4 and Nrp1 recruitment to lipid rafts.
source: Furthermore, cerebral ischemia induced by occlusion led to CRMP4 and Nrp1 recruitment to lipid rafts, which hints that these molecules play a role in mediating signal transduction in response to neuronal damage triggered by ischemia-reperfusion (Whitehead et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: For particular cellular processes like axonal growth, Akt must localize to regions enriched in sphingolipids and cholesterol.
source: Indeed, for particular cellular processes like axonal growth, Akt must localize to regions enriched in sphingolipids and cholesterol (Gao and Zhang, 2008).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Sema3E's axonal growth-promoting activity relies on the PI3K/Akt pathway, leading to downstream phosphorylation-induced inactivation of GSK3β.
source: Sema3E axonal growth-promoting activity relies on the PI3K/Akt pathway, as it leads to downstream phosphorylation-induced inactivation of GSK3β (Bellon et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Sema3A's repulsive activity is associated with sequential phosphorylation of CRMP2 by Cdk5 and then by GSK3β, blocking interaction between CRMP2 and microtubules in DRG-derived neurons.
source: Conversely, Sema3A's repulsive activity was associated with sequential phosphorylation of CRMP2 by Cdk5 and then by GSK3β, blocking interaction between CRMP2 and microtubules in DRG-derived neurons (Uchida et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: GSK3β-dependent phosphorylation of CRMPs can be considered a mechanism regulating CRMP activity in response to the attractive or repulsive effects of guidance molecules.
source: Therefore, GSK3β-dependent phosphorylation of CRMPs can be considered to be a mechanism regulating CRMP activity in response to the attractive or repulsive effects of the guidance molecules.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison of Sema3E and Sema3A signaling mechanisms and their differential effects on CRMP phosphorylation.

claim: CRMP4 phosphorylation may alter its localization rather than its cytoskeleton modulatory function.
source: One explanation for this result could be that CRMP4 phosphorylation alters its localization rather than its cytoskeleton modulatory function. This phosphorylation-dependent localization could have been bypassed following electroporation of CRMP4 plasmids, resulting in ubiquitous overexpression of CRMP4 mutants. This hypothesis has previously been proposed for the response to Sema3D (Tanaka et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is a speculative explanation for the experimental results, supported by a similar hypothesis from previous literature.

claim: The cytoskeleton-binding domain of CRMP4 is required for Sema3E's growth-promoting activity.
source: Finally, we showed that the cytoskeleton-binding domain of CRMP4 is required for Sema3E's growth-promoting activity, suggesting that CRMP4 plays a role at the interface between Sema3E receptors, located in DRM domains, and the cytoskeleton network.
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments showing that CRMP4 lacking the cytoskeleton-binding domain cannot restore Sema3E responsiveness.

claim: The fornix is affected in many psychiatric diseases, such as schizophrenia.
source: As the fornix is affected in many psychiatric diseases, such as schizophrenia, our results provide new insights to better understand the neurodevelopmental components of these diseases.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about fornix involvement in psychiatric diseases.

claim: The post-commissure of the fornix is the major output of the hippocampus and is mainly composed of subicular axons that primarily terminate in the mammillary bodies.
source: The post-commissure of the fornix is the major output of the hippocampus and is mainly composed of subicular axons that primarily terminate in the mammillary bodies (Witter, 2006).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: The post-commissural fornix belongs to a set of limbic connections, including the Papez circuit, involved in memory, emotion, personality, and navigation.
source: The post-commissural fornix belongs to a set of limbic connections, including the Papez circuit, involved in memory, emotion, personality, and navigation (Bubb et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Disruption of the fornix is associated with several psychiatric disorders and neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Disruption of the fornix is associated with several psychiatric disorders and neurodegenerative diseases (Koshiyama et al., 2020; Nowrangi and Rosenberg, 2015).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: The attractive effect of Sema3E on subicular neurons is crucial for fornix development and is enabled by a tripartite receptor complex composed of PlxD1, Nrp1, and VEGFR2.
source: The attractive effect of Sema3E on subicular neurons is crucial for fornix development and is enabled by a tripartite receptor complex composed of plexin-D1 (PlxD1), neuropilin-1 (Nrp1) and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR2) (Bellon et al., 2010; Chauvet et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Nrp1 has been shown to localize to detergent-resistant membrane (DRM) domains (including lipid rafts).
source: Some receptors involved in semaphorin signaling pathways, such as Nrp1, have been shown to localize to detergent-resistant membrane (DRM) domains (including lipid rafts) (Guirland et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Cholesterol- and sphingolipid-enriched DRM domains are involved in axonal growth and guidance, acting as platforms for ligand-induced receptor activation and recruitment of intracellular actors.
source: Cholesterol- and sphingolipid-enriched DRM domains are involved in axonal growth and guidance, acting as platforms for ligand-induced receptor activation and recruitment of intracellular actors (Simons and Sampaio, 2011).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Kinases downstream of semaphorin signaling, such as Akt or GSK3β, can be recruited to DRM domains where they are activated.
source: For example, kinases downstream of semaphorin signaling, such as Akt or glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK3β), can be recruited to DRM domains where they are activated (Gao and Zhang, 2009; Sui et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: The five CRMPs members have been implicated in numerous neuronal processes including neurite outgrowth, dendritic arborization, axonal regeneration, and axonal transport.
source: The five CRMPs members have been implicated in numerous neuronal processes including neurite outgrowth (Ji et al., 2014; Khazaei et al., 2015), dendritic arborization (Niisato et al., 2012; Niisato et al., 2013), axonal regeneration (Alabed et al., 2007; Alabed et al., 2010; Leung et al., 2002), and axonal transport (Kimura et al., 2005; Tsuboi et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: CRMP2 was the first to be implicated in Sema3A-dependent growth cone collapse in higher vertebrates.
source: Within this family, CRMP2 was the first to be implicated in Sema3A-dependent growth cone collapse in higher vertebrates (Goshima et al., 1995) and continues to be the most extensively studied.
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Sema3A stimulates CRMP2 phosphorylation through GSK3β activation which regulates the interaction between CRMP2 and the cytoskeleton.
source: Sema3A stimulates CRMP2 phosphorylation through GSK3β activation which regulates the interaction between CRMP2 and the cytoskeleton (Fukata et al., 2002; Khazaei et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: MAP6 is crucial for fornix development due to its role in regulating axonal elongation induced by Sema3E.
source: Recently, we showed that microtubule-associated protein 6 (MAP6) was crucial for fornix development due to its role in regulating axonal elongation induced by Sema3E (Deloulme et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is based on previous work by the authors cited in the manuscript.

claim: CRMP4 binds the tripartite Sema3E-receptor complex in a DRM domain-dependent manner.
source: The results presented here show that CRMP4 binds the tripartite Sema3E-receptor complex in a DRM domain-dependent manner.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation and sucrose gradient fractionation experiments showing preferential interaction in DRM fractions.

claim: Disruption of DRM domains blocks Sema3E-mediated axonal growth and affects CRMP4 phosphorylation by GSK3β.
source: Disruption of DRM domains blocks Sema3E-mediated axonal growth and affects CRMP4 phosphorylation by GSK3β.
evidence: The claim is supported by experiments showing that MβCD treatment blocks Sema3E-induced axonal growth and prevents changes in CRMP4 phosphorylation.

claim: The integrity of DRM domains is critical for downstream activation of the PI3K/Akt/GSK3β pathway by Sema3E.
source: The integrity of DRM domains is thus critical for downstream activation of the PI3K/Akt/GSK3β pathway by Sema3E.
evidence: The claim is supported by experiments showing that MβCD treatment blocks Sema3E-induced activation of the Akt/GSK3β pathway.

claim: Sema3E signaling triggers a reduction of GSK3β-driven phosphorylation of CRMP4.
source: Furthermore, we found that Sema3E signaling triggers a reduction of GSK3β-driven phosphorylation of CRMP4, and that the interaction of CRMP4 with the cytoskeleton is necessary to transduce Sema3E signaling.
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis showing decreased CRMP4 phosphorylation upon Sema3E treatment.

claim: The interaction of CRMP4 with the cytoskeleton is necessary to transduce Sema3E signaling.
source: Furthermore, we found that Sema3E signaling triggers a reduction of GSK3β-driven phosphorylation of CRMP4, and that the interaction of CRMP4 with the cytoskeleton is necessary to transduce Sema3E signaling.
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments showing that CRMP4 lacking the cytoskeleton-binding domain cannot restore Sema3E responsiveness.

claim: CRMP4 is a downstream effector of the Sema3E signaling pathway, exerting its activity through DRM domains and phospho-regulated interactions with the cytoskeleton.
source: Taken together, our results establish CRMP4 as a new specific downstream effector of the Sema3E signaling pathway, exerting its activity through DRM domains and phospho-regulated interactions with the cytoskeleton.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on multiple experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: DRM/lipid rafts regulate the spatiotemporal recruitment of Sema3E-specific receptors to recruit ubiquitous effectors such as Akt or GSK3β to specific membrane compartments.
source: Our results support the idea that DRM/lipid rafts regulate the spatiotemporal recruitment of Sema3E-specific receptors in order to recruit ubiquitous effectors such as Akt or GSK3β to specific membrane compartments (Averaimo et al., 2016; Lingwood and Simons, 2010).
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the experimental results supported by published literature on DRM/lipid raft function.

claim: CRMP4 is the terminal downstream effector of Sema3E in axonal-growth induction, modulating cytoskeletal dynamics to mediate axonal growth.
source: In summary, we propose that CRMP4 is the terminal downstream effector of Sema3E in axonal-growth induction, modulating cytoskeletal dynamics to mediate axonal growth.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model based on the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: The fornix alterations observed in CRMP4-KO mice may contribute to behavioral defects including decreased social interaction and altered sensory responses.
source: It is therefore possible that the fornix alterations we observed in CRMP4-KO mice here may contribute to these behavioral defects.
evidence: The claim is a speculative connection between the anatomical findings and previously reported behavioral phenotypes.

claim: Recent investigations of white matter microstructure by diffusion tensor imaging across psychiatric disorders have highlighted alterations of the fornix in patients suffering from both schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorders (ASD).
source: This tract is crucial for cognitive functions, and in line with this role, recent investigations of white matter microstructure by diffusion tensor imaging across psychiatric disorders have highlighted alterations of the fornix in patients suffering from both schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorders (ASD) (Koshiyama et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Application of Sema3E (5 nM) to WT cultured subicular neurons 48 hr after electroporation with control siRNA induces a 1.2-fold increase in axon length (120%, p < 0.0001).
source: As previously reported (Chauvet et al., 2007; Deloulme et al., 2015), application of Sema3E (5 nM) to WT cultured subicular neurons 48 hr after electroporation with control siRNA induced a 1.2-fold increase in axon length (Figure 2C and D, 120%, p < 0.0001).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: The number of subicular neurons does not differ in adult WT- and CRMP4-KO brains.
source: Readers should note, the number of subicular neurons does not differ in adult WT- and CRMP4-KO brains (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of eYFP-stained subicular neurons in WT and CRMP4-KO brains.

claim: The pre-commissural fornix and medial cortico-hypothalamic tract show no obvious difference between WT and CRMP4-KO mice.
source: Qualitative analysis of the pre-commissural fornix and mcht, using the hybrid uDISCO clearing method (see Materials and method section) on brains expressing YFP across the fornix system, revealed no obvious difference in these tracts between WT and CRMP4-KO mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by qualitative analysis of cleared brain images.

claim: The post-commissural projection is the main fornix projection altered in CRMP4-KO.
source: These observations suggest that the post-commissural projection is the main fornix projection altered in CRMP4-KO.
evidence: The claim is inferred from observations showing defects in the post-commissural fornix but not in other fornix projections.

claim: The defect in fornix development combined with defasciculation observed in CRMP4-KO mice phenotypically copies the defects observed in Sema3E-KO mice.
source: The defect in fornix development combined with defasciculation observed in CRMP4-KO mice phenotypically copies the defects observed in Sema3E-KO mice (Chauvet et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of the authors' findings with published data on Sema3E-KO mice.

claim: The fornix defects found in single-gene KO and in double heterozygous animals, but not in single heterozygous mice, are strong indicators of an in vivo interaction between Crmp4 and Sema3e during fornix development.
source: The fornix defects found in single-gene KO and in double heterozygous animals, but not in single heterozygous mice, are strong indicators of an in vivo interaction between Crmp4 and Sema3e during fornix development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from genetic interaction studies showing a specific phenotype in double heterozygotes.
